overall: AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: a recess needs no vote, the recording showed no deliberation during the break, and the slander allegation was outside the Law and declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair declared a recess at the December 18 meeting without a formal vote.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, there is no requirement that a public body vote to take a recess.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair conferred with two other members in the hall during the recess, described as a 'huddle', which would be deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As there is no evidence that members of the Board deliberated outside of a meeting, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair deliberated with a member after re-entering the room but before the Board reconvened.
allegations.key_passage: Even if Chair Waygan and member Faulkner discussed business within the Board's jurisdiction during the break, it would not constitute deliberation, as less than a quorum would have been present.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a member made slanderous comments about a resident who had spoken at a public hearing during the break.
allegations.key_passage: Because slander by a Board member, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review this allegation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
